judge.note: generator model not recorded: cross-family judging cannot be established

notes: REPLAY-MODE: provider and judge ran on deterministic doubles; no number here is a live-model result (§10.7 item 9, NFR-REP-01).
RETRIEVAL arms are the eval-side reference implementations (BM25 / hashed-dense / RRF); t5 owns the shipped hybrid retriever and t11 must re-run the evidence arms.
calibration uses the packed evidence score as p̂ (arm hybrid-rrf); the conformal calibrator is t8's and no conformal claim is made here.

16 judge call(s) had a reference answer whose numeric identifiers do not occur anywhere in the corpus; the rubric graded those answers against their cited evidence instead (the reference could not be verified, and grading against it would measure the corpus generator)
position-swap audit: 8/8 comparisons kept their verdict across both orders (invariance 1.00, mean order effect 0.000)
human agreement: no calibration labels on disk (evals/judge/human_v1.jsonl); judged metrics stay not-reportable (§7.5 F-10)

limitations: **Synthetic data optimism.** Queries derive from the corpus and are paraphrased from it; recall and groundedness are therefore optimistic relative to real support traffic. No number here transfers to a production corpus without re-measurement.

**Small n.** A few hundred test items give roughly ±3 points on the macro retrieval metric and much wider intervals on per-locale and subset metrics. Every cell carries n and a CI; a 'win' that does not clear the CI is reported as noise.

**Judge bias.** Judged metrics are LLM-mediated; low-resource languages are likely worse. κ per language is published; where κ < 0.60 the metric is marked 'not reportable' rather than softened with adjectives.
**Benchmark ≠ support domain.** Public leaderboard values are vendor-curated snapshots; an embedder choice is justified only by our own ablation.
**Conformal exchangeability.** The risk guarantee holds under exchangeability. v1.0 has no real traffic, so drift is simulated, not observed.
**Environment dependence.** Latency and cost numbers are for the recorded machine and the pinned pricing table; they are not portable claims.
**No production evidence.** No SLA, no incident history, no live traffic, no measured handoff cost.
**Cache results are replay-based.** The semantic cache belongs to t8; this run measures an exact-normalised-query probe, not a production hit rate.
**Replay mode is labelled.** Any number produced without a live model/provider carries REPLAY-MODE and may never be presented as a live result.
**No claim of SOTA.** The repository claims reproducibility, calibration artifacts and citation verification — not state-of-the-art retrieval or generation.
